items.exemplar:
A. Northern abolitionism — pamphlets, petitions, and orators like William Lloyd Garrison — convinced many Southerners that the North meant to destroy their way of life.

B. The fight over slavery in the territories acquired from Mexico, from the Wilmot Proviso through 'Bleeding Kansas,' turned westward expansion into a sectional battleground.

C. Leaders repeatedly tried compromise: the Missouri Compromise (1820) drew a line at 36°30′, and the Compromise of 1850 patched the Union together for another decade.
parts: A. Briefly explain ONE issue that deepened sectional hostility between North and South in the period 1835–1860.
B. Briefly explain a SECOND such issue.
C. Briefly explain ONE effort to compromise between the sections in this period.
items.stimulus: Historian David Potter describes the 1850s as the decade when 'the slavery question ceased to be a subject of debate and became a test of loyalty' — each section demanding the other prove its good faith.
